A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TrajAgent, with matching core components and identifiable retained experiments. All 14 pages of v2 and 24 pages of v4, including their appendices, support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original trajectory-modeling experiments, agent ablations, sensitivity analyses and automated-method comparisons, including additional GPS results in Appendix A.4.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and adds optimization traces, mitigation comparisons, a score-feedback ablation and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The UniEnv architecture, four-stage workflow and augmentation-then-parameter-optimization loop remain. v4 reports targeted contrastive-reflection and memory-pruning enhancements and specifies GPS/map augmentation using downsampling, constrained noise and temporal checks. Selecting two successful prompt examples already existed in v2; renaming them high-scoring memory entries is not a new component.

E1.justification: Appendix A.6 newly reports S2TUL experiments on FSK-London, whereas the earlier Foursquare population is described as New York City. Table 1 also adds travel-time estimation on Tencent using DutyTTE. The other datasets and task families are retained; adding another TTE model does not itself create a new subtask.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds DutyTTE to the original-versus-optimized model comparisons. New Table 9 compares Llama3-70B, DeepSeek-v3 and Gemini-2.0-flash-001. The existing Optuna/UrbanLLM comparison and comparator membership in Tables 2-4 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New Appendix A.6 studies specify S2TUL step sweeps with memory length 1 and memory sweeps with step 5, alongside a score-removal control. Table 8 introduces cost measurements on 200 trajectories at steps 1 and 5. These are added evaluation designs, without evidence that the retained experiments' protocols changed.

E4.justification: v2 already contained reflection/memory ablations, sensitivity plots and an optimization-trap case study. v4 substantially extends this evidence with operator-selection traces across LLMs, additional memory-length analyses, before/after mitigation comparisons and the score-feedback ablation in Tables 9-13.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or statistical tests. The retained five seed queries concern synthetic query generation, not repeated experimental runs; the new optimization traces do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds GraphMM DA=0.3258 and changes JO from 0.2427 to 0.3422. LLM-ZS gains PO=0.3302, while JO changes from 0.3225 to 0.3350. These accompany expanded optimization configurations, rather than establishing same-setting gains. DutyTTE results and Tables 8-13 add substantial numerical evidence; Tables 2-4 and 7 retain their values.

T1.justification: The optimization formulation in Section 2.1 and the metric definitions in Appendix A.3 are retained. Equation numbering changes, but no new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive mathematical derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the reported improvement range from 2.38%-34.96% to 2.38%-69.91%, and the introduction adds failure-dynamics analysis and robustness improvements as contributions. The central claim of automated, unified trajectory modeling through large-and-small model collaboration remains.

C2.justification: v2 already identified optimization traps and said memory size had little effect on parameter optimization. v4 adds explanations involving local optima, reasoning-model exploration and memory pollution, arguing pruning matters for parameter optimization too. Section 2.4.1 newly interprets score feedback as evidence of causal reasoning, although its claimed below-0.5% no-score improvement conflicts with Table 13.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code/data repository link, Ubuntu/RTX 3090 hardware information, single-GPU small-model training details and token/time costs in Table 8. These are new disclosures, not evidence of changed hardware. Conversely, it removes v2's explicit statement that GPT-4o-mini underlies the Table 4 ablations.

R1.justification: Related Work adds CAMS, AgentMove, CityGPT, UrbanLLaVA and CityBench, and explicitly positions the agent framework against domain-specific LLM fine-tuning. Earlier references are otherwise retained after matching bibliographic changes; the principal unified-modeling positioning remains.

P1.justification: v4 revises the title, condenses experimental discussion, reorganizes Related Work into three topics, and inserts a main-text failure-analysis section and Appendix A.6. Most introductory, methodological and prompt-example wording remains closely matched, so the editorial revision is limited despite the added scientific content.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column ACM layout to a single-column NeurIPS layout. Table 2 rearranges dataset blocks into side-by-side columns; v2 Figure 5 becomes v4 Figure 4(c), and the existing case illustration moves from Figure 6 to Figure 5. Six new appendix tables substantially expand the displays.

improvement.justification: The added operator traces and mitigation comparisons make v2's mainly qualitative failure discussion more inspectable, while hardware, cost and access disclosures improve reproducibility documentation. The net gain is limited by new interpretive errors: Section 2.4.1 claims no-score improvement below 0.5%, but Table 13 shows 56.28% to 63.85%. Incorrect table cross-references further weaken the added analysis.
